question:
(i) Describe the observations made when a bar magnet is moved towards and away from a coil connected to a galvanometer.
(ii) Explain why no deflection is observed when there is no relative motion between the magnet and the coil.
(iii) State the conclusion drawn from these observations.

options.A:
(i) The galvanometer deflects in the same direction for approach and withdrawal.
(ii) It continues to deflect when there is no relative motion.
(iii) A magnetic field alone always produces induced current.
options.B:
(i) No deflection occurs when the magnet moves because the coil is closed.
(ii) Deflection occurs only when both magnet and coil are stationary.
(iii) Current is independent of magnetic flux.
options.C:
(i) Moving the magnet toward the coil gives a momentary deflection; moving it away gives a momentary deflection in the opposite direction.
(ii) With no relative motion the flux is constant, so no deflection occurs.
(iii) Induced current is produced only when the magnetic flux linked with the coil changes.
options.D:
(i) The deflection is greatest when the magnet is held stationary.
(ii) No deflection occurs only if the coil is open.
(iii) Induced current depends only on the magnet’s mass.
